function: Joint communication symbol detection and passive sensing (range, velocity of targets) in an ISAC receiver; a deep-unfolded network learns the iteration hyper-parameters (pp. 8-9).
system: Bistatic passive-sensing ISAC, OFDM MIMO with 8 transmit and 8 receive antennas, 4 GHz, 123 MHz bandwidth, 16-QAM, 1-3 point targets, no RIS (p. 11).
method: Deep-unfolded network (K layers: improved D-AMP detection, 2D-DFT sensing, channel reconstruction), five learnable hyper-parameters per layer; offline training on simulated data, loss not stated (pp. 9-10).
data_channel: Own MATLAB simulation; single-reflection geometric channel with Weibull small-scale fading and point targets; 95% of samples for training, 5% for testing (pp. 5, 10).
test_conditions: Train: simulated data, SNR -20 to 60 dB, parameters per SNR. Test: held-out 5%, 500 Monte Carlo trials per point; one or three targets (pp. 10-14).
baselines: Communication: MAP, OAMP-Net2, TPG, non-unfolded Algorithm 3. Sensing: 2D-DFT and Algorithm 3 (pp. 13-14, Table IV).
metrics: BER and SER for communication; NMSE of range and velocity for sensing; convergence versus number of layers (pp. 11-14).
complexity: Order O(K Lp (NtNr + MN + N log N + M log M + 2NtNr(MN)^2)), counting complex multiplications; no runtime or parameter count (p. 11).
openness: none; data generated by own MATLAB simulation, no code or data link (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 5: "The geometric channel model with single-reflection is adopted as the ISAC channel in this paper"; p. 10: "obtained through MATLAB simulation". Custom simulator with Weibull fading; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "95% of the data is used for training and 5% of the data is used for testing". Figs. 8-10 (pp. 13-14) only sweep the SNR; no other scenario, channel, antenna number or configuration than in training is tested.
q3_support: p. 13: "Fig. 9 compares the BER and SER of MAP [22], OAMP-Net2 [22], Algorithm 3, and ISAC-NET" and "the trainable projected gradient (TPG) algorithm [33] based on model-free DL"; p. 14: "Fig. 10 compares the NMSE of the 2D-DFT algorithm [5] and ISAC-NET".
q4_support: p. 11: "the overall complexity of ISAC-NET can be expressed as O(KLp (Nt Nr + M N + N log(N ) + M log(M ) + 2Nt Nr (M N )2 ))".
q5_support: p. 10: "The training and testing data sets are obtained through MATLAB simulation"; the paper gives no code or data link and no public dataset (only the DOI of the article itself, p. 1).
notes: Eligible: the unfolded network with trained hyper-parameters is learned, acts on detection and sensing (physical layer), has 8x8 antennas and reports simulation results. Area 5 over 1: it detects the data symbols and estimates range and velocity jointly in a communicating system, so it is not sensing alone, and the more specific ISAC area wins. Only five scalar hyper-parameters per layer are learned (p. 10). q3 is met by the communication part (MAP and OAMP-Net2 on BER and SER, p. 13); the sensing part is compared only with non-learned 2D-DFT and Algorithm 3 (p. 14), so the reviewer should confirm. The paper does not use the word supervised and does not state the loss. PDF checked: page 1 holds the title and DOI 10.1109/TCOMM.2024.3375818.
